title: FOOTBALL | Head Coach Jeff Lebby Press Conference - 11/22/26
text: question for coach. We'll start with Steve. >> Coach, we'll start with a couple. I mean, just kind of going back and reviewing maybe specifically the offensive line and special teams play after the changes. How do you feel like those two units performed? >> Yeah, want more out of our group up front. I thought we did some really good things. Again, there were some frustrations in, man, some of the red zone run game that we did not get executed. uh didn't finish in great positions, but we did do some good things. And I thought from a protection standpoint, we were much better uh which we need to build upon that obviously for this Friday. And then, you know, outside of Ant's decision on special teams, thought we did some really good things. The two returns, the field goals, how we kick the ball off. So, some really, really good things. I think we're plus 42 in the hidden yardage had a chance to be a lot more than that if if we don't make that decision. um w with Ant on punt returns. So again, plenty to build on, plenty to work on, plenty to improve on, but I thought our guys played, man, really really hard up front, which was good to see. >> And then secondly, you know, it is rivalry week and it takes on a different intensity. I know, you know, what what's the schedule kind of look like and how do you feel like, you know, the team is ready for this week? >> Yeah, today's Monday, so we're we're rolling. We'll have a walk through here this evening. um again to be able to get on schedule and then as we play it out obviously tomorrow turns into Tuesday and so on and so forth and we'll leave Thursday to head to Tupelo and be ready to roll Friday morning. >> What's it going to take for this offensive line to build off of yesterday's performance enough to be able to win on Friday? >> Yeah, we've got to do a great job taking care of the football. That's where it's going to start and that starts again up front. they don't touch the ball, but we've got to do everything we can to keep the quarterback upright and clean from a pass protection standpoint will be a great challenge. I I don't think there's any doubt the front for Miss is is the best part of their defense. Uh and so for us, man, we're going to have to play really well up front and going to have to be [snorts] better than we've been fundamentally and protect the QB in a great way. And then and when we need to go run the football situationally, we have to go run the football to be able to stay on the field. >> Have you taken any time this last month or two and just kind of thought about the what if of Kamario never getting injured and how this regular season could have gone differently had he been able to play all these games? >> No, I haven't spent any time on that. I mean, I've spent all of my time, my energy trying to get us to continue to play better and go win and get the result that that I want, that we want, that our fan base wants. That's where my focus has been, man. That's it's part of this crazy game that we're blessed to be a part of every single day, but my focus has been on trying to find ways to win. >> Coach, the last two years, obviously, you had to go against Lane, but now you're going against Pete Golding. What have you noticed in the difference in the way that they've been able to play and you guys prepare for a Pingling led miss team versus a link play? >> Yeah, I think when you look at them right now, the record is the record. They've lost two one-score games. They have played really, really well at home outside of the Georgia game. They have that's where they've played their best football. You see a passionate group, a group that plays really hard. Again, their front defensively uh is the best part of their defensive unit and again they've got a quarterback that's as good as there is in America. So again, great challenge. Our guys will be really excited to go play. You were asked about Isaiah Dent at left tackle yesterday and played pretty well and in terms of his [snorts] place and the retention pieces of the younger players on the offensive line, maybe even behind the starters right now. How do you feel going forward with that group? >> Yeah, we we we've got to do what we need to do from an acquisition standpoint, but it's always and forever going to start with retention, retaining the right ones going to be really important going to be really important for us up front. So that's where that piece is. Really proud of Isaiah for the way he did play after going back and looking at the tape. Man, played really really hard a ton again to clean up. Uh but but proud of him and how he did what he did yesterday. >> Coach, with the college football postseason kind of changing and not real sure, does making bowl eligibility feel the same to you and is it as important? >> Yeah, it is as important. There's no question about it. We we need to extend our season. That is a huge deal for us to be able to get the extra practices uh to be able to man go play one more one more game and give us an opportunity to go win. So it's a huge deal to me. It's a huge deal to our guys and uh that's just one more added bonus for us for Friday morning. >> Yesterday you talked about how the pass defense needs to be better. Just what kind of things does this defense need to be better at just to be good enough to win on Friday? >> Yeah, again in the manto man world we've got to, you know, we've got to go make the play. when the ball's in the air, it's got to be us making the play. That that'll be a big part of it. And then in zone coverage, we got to take some some air out of it and not uh give these guys all this access even when we are in, you know, our zone uh concept. So, it it's both ways. Um got great confidence with with who we're playing on the perimeter. Uh those guys got to play really really well for us on Friday morning. >> Steve, we'll go with a couple. Trinidad is a guy obviously that can improvise. He's very difficult to get on the ground. I think he's only been sacked 14 times this year. I mean, when you have a quarterback like that that even if you call the right play, he can elude you. How do you kind of defense that? >> Yeah, for us it's about tackling and we have to do a great job of tackling in space. uh when you get a matchup like this, those are the offset plays that man, you again, you can coach uh this a lot of different ways, but the simplicity is is it comes down to tackling and and we have to do a great job of running to the football. We've got to do a great job of winning the one-on- ones and and finding ways to to tackle really well Friday morning. >> Kind of piggybacking off Sam's question, uh you know, life kind of teach us that wisdom and and struggles are inseparable. you know, when you think about this year and kind of taking an inventory, what do you feel like maybe you've learned as a person and as a football coach this year? >> Yeah, I think for me it's man that through the struggles, it's still about creating consistency. Creating consistency for these young guys. Uh it's finding ways to try to create advantage when we're completely different than maybe we were the first four weeks of the season and how we need to do what we do. And so that again, that's that's why they call you coach. You've got to find ways to put guys in positions of success. And for me, there's been great challenge in that, you know, throughout this stretch. And so, none more important than Friday morning. You know, I got to do a great job putting our offense in position to go win our football team as well. But that'll be uh that'll be my stress and my strain this week. >> And with the miss offense, obviously Trinidad's back, but they got a lot of new pieces around him. Is that offense a whole lot different than what you faced last year or is it kind of just the same revolving around Trinidad? >> Yeah, I mean there's a there are there's a ton of similarities. There's some wrinkles that that maybe are a little different conceptually, but again with that guy as the trigger man, he can do so many things. He makes all these off schedule plays, but he really does he makes all the routine plays over and over and over. And so that's what makes it as hard as anything. The off schedule plays are one thing, but all of the routine plays that this guy constantly makes uh puts a lot of stress on you. >> You worked with John David Baker when when you were at Old Miss. What's the biggest difference between him as a play caller versus you versus Lane versus maybe Charlie Weiss. What's What's the difference systematically or however you want to put it? Yeah, I think maybe the biggest difference is he was really raised air raid and uh so that there are some things conceptually in the throw game that's a little bit different. Um again, there are a ton of similarities. the base of the offense again as he went to East Carolina to be the coordinator there and has came came back to Oxford the base of it there are there's a a bunch of of similarities but I think just as he was raised in it that's probably where the biggest difference is >> a couple items here one we saw I guess did not see several guys walk yesterday like Isaac uh Anthony others when do you want them to ideally make their decisions what they're doing so you can plan on either replacing them or moving forward with them. >> Yeah. In in talks obviously right now uh and and then over the next two to three weeks be really important to be able to nail down exactly where we're at with a few of these guys. The walking on senior day is for me just as we move forward it will be about guys that are out of eligibility and so that's why that happened yesterday. >> Canon did not walk but did he did he walk the previous year? >> He did. Okay. >> Yeah he did. And moving to another thing, talking about the bowl, if it turns out that you get an invitation at five and seven something, even without a Camaro, you still want to proceed with the bowl for for the practice and the evaluation purposes for the future. >> Yeah, we'll we'll cross that bridge once we get there. The plan is to find a way to get to six and and that uh that's where our focus is. You talked about Tren Chambless a few minutes ago, but um going against him last year, what did you learn from that match up that you're going to apply to to Friday's game? >> Yeah, again, I think you can sit in here and coach talk all we want about getting the guy on the ground and tackling and not giving him the ability to take the game over. It's it's about doing it on Friday morning. And um again, for us, the way we cage rush, the the way we have great discipline in our rush lanes will be a huge part of it. We have to tackle well, and we've got to get 11 hats to the football. And it is it's that simple. And and again, that's what it will come down to to try to limit him as much as we possibly can. >> Coach Ethan Pull, you only had to punt him one time officially. of course had to the run into the kicker that that wiped out one of them, but and I know you prefer him not to be punting very much. Just talk about his progress this year and how he's helped you uh field position wise. >> Yeah, he has. He's he's gotten better. Uh there were some tough moments in a couple of games. Proud of him for being [clears throat] able to get through that and bounce back to being who we've expected him to be and and has done some really really good things for us. So, from a field position standpoint, going to need that in a great way on Friday, we'll be a huge part of this football game and uh when when Ethan runs out there, got great confidence in him to do what he needs to do for us. >> It's obviously been harder for you guys to score from far since September, but this miss defense does have a propensity to give up explosive plays. Just how do you balance just keeping the offense moving and keeping the chains going with perhaps taking advantage of whatever opportunities they might give you? >> Yeah, we we do. We need to be really good on first and second down, but we do have to create chunks. I mean, that that will be a big part of it. To me, that happens if we have the ability to hold on to the ball for a little bit. And so, us being able to squeeze the ball long enough at times to give our guys the opportunities to go win on the perimeter will be important. That's why I mentioned like the ball security piece, taking care of the ball, it's going to start with us from a protection standpoint up front, playing really clean and and fundamentally playing well. So, um, again, we're [snorts] going to need the chunks on Friday to go do what we need to do. >> With Billy playing on Saturday, does that maybe factor in at all with the quarterback decision even if AJ can come back or just building week to week? Is that is that part of it for you? >> Yeah, I it will really depend on how AJ's able to practice this week. If he's able to really go tomorrow uh to be able to get to work, then I I'll start getting closer to making that decision. Um, but that's that's really what it's going to be about is if he can go practice. I if AJ can't practice at all for us this week, I think it's going to be really hard for him to just go play. So, we'll work through that as we move through the week. >> Appreciate it.
